subject: Supplier onboarding: legal-entity PO identifier, invoice cadence and net-term tradeoffs
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@hearthhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@hearthhealth.com
Date: 2027-02-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Supplier setup: PO metadata + invoice cadence options

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. Procurement is starting the supplier setup and we need a clear list of PO/invoice expectations from Redwood to feed into our ERP. To speed this up can you confirm the following items and any constraints they create on pricing/discounts: 

- Required PO fields on every invoice (PO number in header, PO line -> GL mapping, acceptance code).
- Whether Redwood can accept multiple POs for different Hearth legal entities and have line-level entity-code suffixes in the invoice.
- Invoice cadence options: we prefer weekly or biweekly but can do monthly if needed — what impacts do each cadence choices have on unit pricing or early-pay discounts?
- Net terms flexibility: Procurement prefers Net60 or Net75 for our larger partners; we need to understand price/discount tradeoffs with longer terms.

Attached is our supplier onboarding checklist and a sample W9. We also need a stubbed PO template back so AP can validate field mappings.

Appreciate a brief note — we are trying to onboard before the next procurement cutover (02/15).

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement
Hearth & Health, Inc.
[attachment: procurement_checklist.pdf (PDF)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-03T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Supplier setup: PO metadata + invoice cadence options

Hi Liam — thanks, and great to meet today. Quick answers inline and next steps at the bottom.

1) Required PO fields: PO number in invoice header (exact match), PO line description, SKU/service code, quantity, unit price, tax id for vendor entity, and a single acceptance code field per invoice. We can also include a custom entity-code suffix on line items if your ERP requires it.

2) Multiple POs / legal entities: Yes — we can accept separate POs per Hearth legal entity. We ask that each invoice reference a single Redwood billing entity per invoice (one legal vendor tax id per invoice). If you need multiple vendor tax ids on a single invoice we will need a split-invoice approach (one PDF per vendor tax id) — we can automate this but there is operational overhead.

3) Invoice cadence impact on pricing: Our standard commercial program assumes monthly invoicing with Net45 and a volume discount schedule. Moving to weekly/biweekly increases processing overhead and reduces the finance flexibility that underpins our volume discount model. Practically: 
- Monthly + Net45: standard list pricing + applicable volume discount.
- Biweekly + Net60: list pricing, volume discount may be reduced by 1-3 percentage points depending on committed volume.
- Weekly + Net75: we'd likely need to eliminate early-pay/volume discounts (no additional reduction) unless a prepayment or committed-advance schedule is agreed.

4) Net terms: we can offer Net60 for the pilot but discounts will be reduced. If Hearth can commit to a 12-month minimum spend band or a partial prepay tranche we can preserve most discounts.

Attachments: I attached our supplier PO template and a short field-map csv to show the line-level fields we emit.

Next steps (proposed):
- Liam: confirm which legal entities will be invoicing and whether you require consolidated monthly statements per parent or separate per-entity statements.
- Procurement: confirm preferred cadence (biweekly vs monthly) — if biweekly, we will send an updated pricing matrix that shows the adjusted discount bands.
- Ben / Priya (cc): can you validate finance acceptance for Net60 with a 1-2% discount reduction and flag any further constraints?

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: PO_template_HearthHealth.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-04T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Supplier setup: PO metadata + invoice cadence options

Priyom — quick finance read: 

- Net60 is acceptable for onboarding for this account but with the understanding that our standard volume discounts will step down. For a pilot-sized commitment (under $250k ARR) expect a 1.5–2.5 percentage-point reduction on the headline discount bands.
- Net75 or weekly invoicing materially hurts cash flow, so finance will require either (a) a prepay tranche equal to 25% of the first quarter ARR or (b) removal of any early-pay/volume discounts.
- Operational request: if Hearth requires line-level entity suffixes, ops will need the sample EDI mapping (CSV) up-front and at least one sample test invoice to validate parsing.

If they can accept Net60 + biweekly (instead of weekly) we can provide an adjusted pricing matrix and keep most concessions.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
[attachment: sample_edi_field_map.csv (CSV)]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@hearthhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Bryant <aisha.bryant@hearthhealth.com>, procurement@hearthhealth.com
Date: 2027-02-04T14:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Supplier setup: PO metadata + invoice cadence options

Thanks — that is helpful. A few clarifications from Procurement: 

- We will onboard two Hearth legal entities for this contract (Hearth & Health US, Hearth & Health Inc. UK will be a later phase). For the initial go-live we need separate invoices per vendor tax id (per your guidance) and a consolidated monthly statement that ties those invoices to master POs for our control accountants.
- Biweekly cadence is our preferred compromise (we'd like biweekly payment runs). If you can show the adjusted pricing matrix for Biweekly + Net60 we can route to the budget owner.
- We can do a 12-month minimum spend commitment to preserve more favorable pricing, but need to see the precise discount bands tied to commitment levels.

I attached our W9 and a sample PO export from our ERP that shows the entity suffix usage. Also can we get a DocuSign link for standard SOW + commercial terms so legal can start redlines?

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement
Hearth & Health, Inc.
[attachment: vendor_w9.pdf (PDF)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-05T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Supplier setup: PO metadata + invoice cadence options

Liam — great, thank you. Confirming next steps so we can keep the cutover timeline: 

1) We will provide an adjusted pricing matrix for Biweekly + Net60 showing the discount step-downs and an alternative that preserves discounts with a 12-month minimum commitment. Expect the matrix by EOD 02/06.

2) Engineering/ops will validate the sample PO export you attached — Ben, ops to schedule a test invoice parse on Monday.

3) DocuSign: sending standard SOW + commercial terms now (DocuSign link included below). Please have legal start redlines and route the HubSpot deal to 'Contract review' when ready.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/pack/abcd-1234-setup
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/48271

Attachments we will upload to your onboarding folder: PO_template_HearthHealth.pdf, sample_edi_field_map.csv, and an adjusted pricing matrix (to follow).

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
